chapter: Big band, Chicago players, recordings and gospel
title: The 1968 New Orleans jazz festival on the riverboat President
summary: He went with Art Hodes, with Sharkey Bonano, Peewee Russell and Bob Haggart, playing on a packed steamboat.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: And we find it so different, and when I was down in New Orleans here in '68, I was at the first jazz festival they had. I went down with Art Hodes.
And so they had three bands on this boat. They had Sharky Bananas, then they had Peewee out of New York, and then Sharky was from New Orleans. And then our band from Chicago.
Peewee Russell, right. And he had -- what's his name, playing bass with him, the --
No, no, Peewee, the band he had, the group out of --

Bob Haggart, yeah, right, playing bass with him, and then Sharky Bananas had his band. So we went down there and we played on the boat, and whats' name, George Brunis was with us, yeah. But it was really amazing, to see these people bringing food, and I saw the biggest tambourine I've ever seen in my life -- about that big.
Right, yeah. And they would be -- that boat was rocking. They had over 2,000 people on there. The President was the name of the boat.
Right, have you? Right. And, boy, I'm telling you, they went out -- I mean, down the Mississippi there at night. It was a midnight to 11:00, 12:00 thing, and it was really something.
Yeah, that's a Streckfuss line. I think Streckfuss
Is that-- oh, yeah? Oh, yeah?
-- still in business. Yeah, it's one of the old boats. Big boat.
Right, right, right, big boat, right.
